terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, deponent, with the accusative
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.122: est igitur adulēscentis majōrēs nātū verērī
Cic. Planc. 29: quem verētur ut deum
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to feel awe of, to reverence, revere, respect; to fear” (milder than metuō); frequent in Cicero, while Caesar, Livy and Sallust use only the participle veritus.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 13.78.1: mēque praeter cēterōs et colit et observat et dīligit
terms.comment: Often paired with colō, honour: colere et observāre. For keeping to a rule, see respect (keep to).

terms.gloss: respect, the deference shown to elders and superiors
evidence: Cic. Inv. 2.66: observantiam, per quam aetāte aut sapientiā aut honōre aut aliquā dignitāte antecēdentēs verēmur et colimus
Cic. Off. 1.99: adhibenda est igitur quaedam reverentia adversus hominēs
Juv. 14.47: maxima dēbētur puerō reverentia (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Rare until after the Augustan age (Lewis & Short); Juvenal’s line is the famous one: the greatest respect is owed to a child.

evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 6: L. Sullā, quem honōris causā nōminō
terms.comment: The courtesy with which an orator names a great man: “whom I mention with all respect”. Lewis & Short: “out of respect, in order to show honor”.
Classically a valuation, an assessment of worth (Cicero); Traupman gives it for esteem.

terms.gloss: hold in high esteem, think highly of
terms.grammar: genitive of value: magnī, plūris, maximī facere
evidence: Quint. 11.1.38: negat sē magnī facere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The genitive gives the value set on someone: aliquem maximī facere, to hold someone in the highest esteem; nihilī facere, to care nothing for.

phrases.latin: Est igitur adulēscentis majōrēs nātū verērī exque iīs dēligere optimōs et probātissimōs, quōrum cōnsiliō atque auctōritāte nītātur
phrases.english: It is the part of a young man, then, to respect his elders and to choose from among them the best and most approved, on whose advice and authority he may rely

phrases.latin: summa in hospitēs līberālitās et observantia, mēque praeter cēterōs et colit et observat et dīligit
phrases.english: the greatest generosity and courtesy towards guests; and he honours, respects and loves me more than anyone

phrases.latin: adhibenda est igitur quaedam reverentia adversus hominēs et optimī cujusque et reliquōrum
phrases.english: we must therefore show a certain respect towards people, both the best of them and all the rest
to hold someone in high (the highest) esteem
